subject: separate core and full analyses with exon arrays

messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: separate core and full analyses with exon arrays
parts:
Hi Ken,

If you want to compare analyses from using just the core versus just
the full .cdf for the exon arrays, can you do that? It seems like when
you run the RMA model (after changing the cdf file from core to full,
say) it will just write over the previous fits since the tags would be
the same.

In which case, it seems that you would have to do all of the analysis
on one, and then repeat, but couldn't do side-by-side comparisons as
you go along. I guess you could manually move the files with the fits
from the core and full to another directory and move them to the
correct directory when you want to run the analysis so you didn't have
to wait to refit everytime. Would you get into any problems doing
this? (other than the obvious problem that you might forget and mess
up)

Thanks,
Elizabeth

messages.author: 0e065001d5e74ca3
messages.subject: Re: separate core and full analyses with exon arrays
parts:
> If you want to compare analyses from using just the core versus just
> the full .cdf for the exon arrays, can you do that? It seems like when
> you run the RMA model (after changing the cdf file from core to full,
> say) it will just write over the previous fits since the tags would be
> the same.

You're right that this will happen. To avoid it, you could add some tags
to your initial data set, which should carry through the analysis. e.g.

csFull <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("myDataSet", chipType="HuEx-1_0-st-v2,full", tags="full")

This should work and is much safer than moving files around.

Cheers,

Ken

Hmm... When saving results in subdirectories I strip of any tags from
the chip type, e.g. instead of Mapping250K_Nsp,monocell/, I save as
Mapping250K_Nsp/. Stripping of "monocell" should be fine, but maybe
that is also it. When I made this decision, I did not think of cases
like yours. I will think about the consequences of just stripping of
"monocell".

For now, Ken's suggestion will do.

Cheers

Henrik
